answer: The jury's own reward depends on rejecting low-quality answers, creating a shared incentive among honest graders to spot coordinated fakery, so a Sybil cluster collapses under the weight of its own low scores. The system stays honest because reputation is unforgeable and only earned through accepted attestations, so freshly minted aliases genuinely cannot swing a verdict. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a fable as the anchor of the cost.
